item.title: The definitive guide to London's best afternoon teas
item.description: There's an afternoon tea for everyone — from gluten-free to art-inspired — if you know where to look. Here are some of our tried and tested favourites.

item.title: 22 charming country properties, from £350,000 to £2.5 million, as seen in Country Life
item.description: From a glorious mansions to charming cottages — and everything in between — in this week's round-up.

item.title: How do you make an 18th century stately home fit for a 21st-century family?
item.description: Grace McCloud talks to Toddy Fleming of Studio Cameron about gently updating The Hirsel — a Category A Listed stately home on land in the Scottish Borders that's been occupied by the same family for nearly a millennium.

item.title: Eve Myles: ‘You wouldn't believe how many Emily Blunt pictures get sent to me to sign’
item.description: The Torchwood actor on meeting Linda Hamilton, being the 'best-kep secret in Wales', the book that inspired her to get into acting —and her consuming passions.

item.title: The Suffolk house where two of the greatest women in British history spent their childhood years
item.description: The Suffragette leader Millicent Fawcett and Britain's first female doctor, Elizabeth Garrett Anderson, grew up in this home in Aldeburgh.

item.title: From the Wild West to West London: The indomitable rise of cowboy core
item.description: Dressing like a cowboy has never been more fashionable. Hayley Bloomingdale investigates what's behind the the creeping influence of Americana, in the UK and around the world.

item.title: Colour photographs of Gertrude Jekyll’s garden, rediscovered in the Country Life Archive, offer a rare glimpse of what it looked like at the peak of her fame
item.description: In 1997, Country Life published a set of chromatic photographs of Gertrude Jekyll’s Munstead Wood garden that had lain undisturbed in our archive for nearly a century. We have reproduced the pictures, corresponding feature and captions here.

item.title: From palaces to football pitches, the women devoted to their dogs
item.description: Corgis, spaniels, Dalmatians and celebrity chihuahuas — this International Women’s Day we celebrate some of the women whose devotion to their dogs is almost as well known as they are.

item.title: At war in a foreign country, jailed by your own son and traded as a teenager as part of a business proposition: The ladies of Leeds Castle saw it all
item.description: Laura Kay charts the remarkable history of ‘The Ladies' Castle’ near Maidstone, Kent.

item.title: What is everyone talking about this week: The man creating the new Turner Prize
item.description: Louis Elton, an alumnus of both Oxford and Cambridge, believes innovative artisanship is the answer to Britain's challenges. Now, he's launching a prize for what he calls the country's 'misfit makers'.
